html.body: Date: 2025-04-02 REMARKSI. INTRODUCTIONApplicant thanks the Examiner for the indication of allowable subject matter in claims 1-2 and 4-10. Applicant has amended claims 1-2 and 6. Accordingly, claims 1-2 and 4-10 are presently pending in this application. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application in view of the foregoing amendments and the following arguments.II. REJECTION OF CLAIMS 1-2 AND 4-10 UNDER 35 U.S.C. § 112 Claims 1-2 and 4-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite.Applicant has amended claims 1-2 and 6 and respectfully submits that the rejection of claims 1-2 and 4-10 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) has been overcome.In claim 1, the Examiner asserts that the language "various coil units (101) of the first coil (6) are combined to form" and "various coil units (101) of the second coil (7) are combined to form" is indefinite because it is unclear if the language is directed to manufacturing of the device and an intermediate product or attempts to define a final structural element of the device. Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 2, lines 17-24.Applicant has amended the language to recite "the first coil (6) comprises various coil units (101) configured as a sleeve structure..." and "the second coil (7) comprises various coil units (101) configured as a curved triangular structure..." to clarify that the limitations define structural elements.Also in claim 1, the Examiner asserts that the language "an exhaust hole (9) is formed" is indefinite because it is unclear if the language is directed to manufacturing of the device and an intermediate product or attempts to define a final structural element of the device. Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 3, lines 1-4. Applicant has amended the language to recite "the negative pressure cylinder (2) is provided with an exhaust hole (9)..." to clarify that the limitation defines a structural element.Also in claim 1, the Examiner asserts that the language "by setting programmed negative pressure suction pressures with different magnitudes and rates by the controller (12), blood flow velocity of a penile blood vessel is adjusted to achieve non-invasive cavernous arteriovenous network angiography under magnetic resonance imaging of the penis site, thus evaluating the degree of stenosis and occlusion function of cavernous arteriovenous network" is indefinite because it is unclear if the limitation intended to refer to a specific controller/processor type limitation which describes the function of the controller. Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 3, lines 5-13. Applicant has amended the language in accordance with the Examiner's suggestion to recite "the controller (12) is configured to set programmed negative pressure suction pressures with different magnitudes and rates, so as to adjust blood flow velocity of a penile blood vessel..." to clarify the recitation of the invention.Also in claim 1, the Examiner asserts that the language "a contrast agent injection hole (8) is formed" is indefinite because it is unclear if the language is directed to manufacturing of the device and an intermediate product or attempts to define a final structural element of the device. Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 3, lines 16-20.Applicant has amended the language to recite "...one side of a front end of the negative pressure cylinder (2) is provided with a contrast agent injection hole (8), ..." to clarify that the limitation defines a structural element.Also in claim 1, the Examiner asserts that the language "and when non-invasive angiography under the magnetic resonance imaging is poor, a magnetic resonance contrast agent is able to be injected into corpus cavernosum via a connecting pipe through the full-automatic magnetic resonance contrast agent injection system for further development and angiography of the penile blood vessel" is indefinite because it is unclear if the limitation is intended to refer to a specific controller/processor type limitation which describes the function of the injection system processor/controller.Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 3, line 21 to p. 4, line 4. Applicant has amended the language in accordance with the Examiner's suggestion to recite "...the full- automatic magnetic resonance contrast agent injection system is configured to inject a magnetic resonance contrast agent into corpus cavernosum via a connecting pipe when non-invasive angiography under the magnetic resonance imaging is poor for further development and angiography of the penile blood vessel" to clarify the recitation of the invention.In claim 2, the Examiner asserts that the language "is that a through hole is formed" is unclear. Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 4, lines 8-9. Applicant has amended claim 2 to recite "... a central part of the shield (10) is provided with a through hole" to clarify the recitation of the invention.In claim 6, the Examiner asserts that the language "is in manual control" is indefinite because it is unclear what further structure is intended by the language. Office Action of January 27, 2025 at p. 4, lines 10-12. Applicant has amended claim 6 to recite "...wherein the first butterfly needle valve is configured to be controlled manually, and the second butterfly needle valve is configured to be controlled manually or controlled by the controller" to clarify the recitation of the invention.Applicant respectfully submits that claims 1-2 and 4-10, as amended, recite a definite invention and that the rejection of claims 1-2 and 4-10 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) has been overcome. Applicant therefore requests that the rejection of claims 1-2 and 4- 10 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be withdrawn.III. CONCLUSIONFor the above cited reasons, all of the claims presently pending in this application are believed to be allowable. If the Examiner has any further questions or concerns, the Examiner is invited to contact the Applicant's undersigned attorney.Respectfully submitted, /William F. Kolakowski III/ William F.
